name: Elevate Mystery Shopping
tierRationale: Directly competitive by service, but there is no public evidence yet of deal presence, client base or capacity. Watchlist until it shows up in a real opportunity.
posture: Monitor. Do not build enablement until it appears in a deal.

verdict.line: A new, founder-led shop provider selling multifamily credibility rather than scale — it competes on who reads the report, so the contest is coverage, comparability and what happens after the shop.

stackLayer.name: Resolution · The Resolution Layer for Multifamily
stackLayer.note: Competes for the resolution layer position, or for one slice of it.

founded.value: Not published. Surfaced in the Grace Hill competitive channel on 17 July 2026 as a new company.

ownership.value: Founder-owned. Eric Franco, Founder & Director of Training.

size.value: Unknown — no team page, shopper network size or coverage map is published.

pricing.value: Not published. Customized scoring criteria are stated as included at no additional cost.

positioning.value: Positions itself as going beyond scoring — it 'connects evaluation findings to coaching, training, and measurable results' to help teams 'convert more prospects into residents'. Serves multifamily residential exclusively.

strengths.text: Founder brings 20+ years in multifamily, from leasing agent to regional leadership, including systems training and performance improvement — credibility with the buyer is his core asset.
Multifamily-exclusive. No retail or restaurant business diluting the rubric.
Eight shop types published, including new-construction lease-up shops and competitive shops — a wider published menu than most new entrants.
Customized scoring criteria included with every shop at no additional cost — removes the setup-fee objection a buyer may have hit elsewhere.
Every evaluation ships with a 13-page report, a 'Leasing Decision Journey' framework and a 30-day improvement blueprint.
Offers a Follow-Up Shop roughly 30 days after the evaluation, explicitly to measure whether coaching changed behavior — a closed loop most shop vendors do not sell.

gaps.text: No shopper network size, geographic coverage or capacity is published anywhere on the site — the practical question for a multi-state portfolio is unanswered.
No named clients, testimonials or case studies are published.
No industry benchmark dataset is described — scoring is customized per client, which by design makes results comparable within an account but not against the wider industry.
No pricing, turnaround time, or shopper recruitment method is published.
No third-party coverage, trade press, review-site presence or funding record could be found in an August 2026 search — the only public footprint is the company's own site.

whyWeWin: Benchmarking. Customized scoring is a real selling point for them and the exact thing that prevents an industry comparison — ask what a score of 87 means against anyone but themselves.

Scale and continuity. Ellis and EPMS are Grace Hill companies with decades of shopping behind them; a founder-led firm's capacity and coverage across a multi-state portfolio is an open question worth asking about plainly.

The loop is already built. Their follow-up shop measures whether coaching landed; ours routes a low score into an assigned course and re-measures inside the same platform, with no second vendor and no manual handoff.
One contract. A buyer comparing shops alone is comparing one line item — shops sitting next to training, policy, surveys and reputation is a different purchase.
askThis: How many shoppers do you have in the markets where my properties actually are, and what's your monthly capacity across the portfolio?
If my scoring criteria are custom to me, what do I compare my results against outside my own portfolio?
Who does the work if you're unavailable for a month — what's the bench?
When a shop comes back low, what actually assigns the training and proves the score moved?
doNotSay: Do not disparage the founder or imply a small firm can't deliver a good shop. Twenty years of multifamily operations is real credibility and the buyer may know him personally — attacking it will cost you the room.
Do not claim they can't do video, lease-up or competitive shops. All eight shop types are published on their site.
Do not quote or guess their pricing. None is published.
Do not present the absence of named clients as proof they have none — it is an absence of public evidence, and say it that way.

whenItComesUp.why: A new entrant selling operator credibility rather than infrastructure. It competes for the shop line item, and it will be attractive to a buyer who has been burned by a big vendor's generic rubric. The open questions are capacity, comparability and continuity — not competence.
whenItComesUp.say: If you know Eric, that experience is worth something — a shop report written by someone who has actually run a region reads differently, and I wouldn't argue with that. The questions I'd want answered are practical: coverage in your markets, what you benchmark the score against, and what happens after the report lands.
whenItComesUp.avoid: Don't attack the founder or the size of the business. It reads as threatened, and if the buyer has a relationship with him you've lost the conversation rather than the deal.
whenItComesUp.redirect: When a shop comes back low, what happens next in your world — who gets told, what training gets assigned, and how do you know it improved?

spiced.listenFor: They name Elevate or mention 'someone from the industry' who has started a shopping company.
spiced.ask: Who are you using for shops today, and how did you come across them?

spiced.listenFor: Frustration with a previous vendor's generic rubric or shopper quality — that is usually what makes a founder-led firm attractive.
spiced.ask: What wasn't working about how shops were being run before?

spiced.listenFor: Whether they can compare scores across properties and against the industry, or only within their own portfolio.
spiced.ask: When you see a score, what do you compare it to — last quarter, the property next door, or the industry?

spiced.listenFor: A lease-up, a new-construction delivery or a fair housing concern driving urgency.
spiced.ask: What's driving the timing — a lease-up, an audit, or something that happened?

spiced.listenFor: Whether shops are a standalone line item or part of a wider performance conversation.
spiced.ask: Is this a shopping decision on its own, or part of a broader look at how you measure and improve onsite performance?

ms-human-shoppers.note: Human evaluation is implied throughout, but no shopper network, size or recruitment method is described.

ms-phone.note: Phone Shops — greeting and tone, rapport, needs discovery, community presentation, objection handling, appointment setting, follow-up commitment.

ms-email.note: Email & Text Response Evaluations — response time, personalization, value communication, CTA clarity, follow-up cadence, brand voice.

ms-onsite.note: Onsite Leasing Shops covering curb appeal through application guidance.

ms-video.note: Video Mystery Shops evaluating body language, tour presentation and non-verbal communication.

ms-rubric.note: Scoring is customized per client at no extra cost. Consistent within an account; a custom rubric is not a standardized one.

ms-coaching.note: A 30-day improvement blueprint and a Follow-Up Shop measure whether coaching landed, but there is no linked training assignment — the coaching is advisory.

ms-full-call-analysis.note: Sampled human shops, not analysis of every call.

ms-benchmarking.note: No industry benchmark dataset is described. Customized scoring implies within-account comparison only.

objections.objection: He actually ran properties — he understands this better than a big vendor.
objections.response: That's fair, and I'd say the same. What one experienced person gives you is a better-written report. What you also need is enough shoppers to cover your markets every month, a score that means something outside your own portfolio, and something that assigns the fix and checks it worked. Ask him those three, then ask us.

news.headline: New multifamily mystery shopping company surfaces: Elevate Mystery Shopping
news.impact: Shared in #industry-competitive_intel. Founded by a former Director of Training at a multifamily operator. No third-party coverage yet.
